title: REAL-TIME UPDATES
subtitle: Push changes to clients the moment they happen, even when the sender and receiver are connected to different servers.

items: Users expect to see changes within about a second: chat, live comments, prices, collaboration, ride tracking.
Polling would be mostly empty responses or far too frequent.
Polling: simple, but latency = interval and most requests return nothing. Fine for slow updates (every ~30s).
Server push: SSE (server→client, plain HTTP, auto-reconnect) or WebSocket (bidirectional). Long-polling is the fallback.
With many servers, the receiver's connection lives on another server than the one that got the event.
Pub/sub routes events to whichever servers hold the interested connections: channel per video, per user, or per symbol.
How fresh must it be? Every 30 s or slower: just poll.
Server-to-client only? Use Server-Sent Events (plain HTTP, auto-reconnect).
Both directions, low latency? Use WebSockets.
Many servers? Route events with pub/sub (Redis, Kafka) to whichever server holds the connection.
Can events be lost? If not, persist first and let clients resume from an offset after reconnecting.

blocks.text: "Viewers only receive, so SSE is enough. Each comment is published once to a channel per video; every server holding viewers of that video is subscribed and pushes it to them."

items: Assuming sender and receiver share a server.
No plan for reconnects and missed messages.

blocks.text: Used in: Ride sharing (Uber), Live comments (Facebook Live), Collaborative editor (Google Docs), Stock trading (Robinhood), Online auction, LLM chat (ChatGPT), Chat app (WhatsApp)
